blocks.text: Tacoma Condos & Townhomes Exterior: Best Paint Colors

When it comes to Tacoma condos or townhomes exterior painting, choosing the right colors is more than just a matter of taste, it’s about enhancing curb appeal, staying COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA-compliant, and making your property stand out for the right reasons. Whether you’re updating your own unit or part of a board overseeing a larger complex, the exterior colors you select impact property value, neighborhood cohesion, and long-term satisfaction.

In this guide, we’ll walk you through the essential steps to selecting the best paint colors for condos and townhomes exterior in Tacoma, with a focus on current trends, architectural compatibility, and coordination with your homeowner’s association.

blocks.text: Why Exterior Color Matters for Condos and Townhomes

Your home’s exterior is the first thing people see and for condos and townhomes, which often share walls or uniform design elements, it’s essential that colors complement both the architecture and the community.
Here’s why making the right choice matters:

items: Curb Appeal: Fresh, modern color can make your unit look new again.
Resale Value: Homes with attractive, on-trend colors often sell faster and for more.
Community Cohesion: Colors should harmonize with neighboring units while still offering individuality.
COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA Requirements: Most communities have rules regarding paint colors—some even provide approved palettes.

blocks.text: 2025 Exterior Paint Trends from Sherwin-Williams
Looking to stay on-trend while maintaining classic appeal? Here are the top Sherwin-Williams color trends for 2025 that are perfect for townhomes and condos in the Tacoma area:
Earthy Neutrals
Warm tones like Shiitake SW 9173, Accessible Beige SW 7036, and Homburg Gray SW 7622 evoke a grounded, natural look that’s timeless and COA/TOA/HOA-friendly.
Crisp Whites and Creams
Clean, fresh, and ideal for modern or craftsman-style architecture, colors like Alabaster SW 7008 and Greek Villa SW 7551 remain popular for trim and siding.
Pacific Northwest-Inspired Hues
Shades that echo our lush environment, like Evergreen Fog SW 9130 or Rain SW 6219, work beautifully in Tacoma’s landscape.
Pro Tip: When in doubt, choose a neutral base and accent with darker trim to highlight architectural details while staying within most COA/TOA/HOA standards.

blocks.text: Step-by-Step: How to Choose the Best Exterior Paint Colors
Here’s a clear process to make your paint color decision smooth, COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA-compliant, and stress-free.
Step 1: Check COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA Guidelines
Start by requesting your COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA’s approved color list. Some associations allow homeowner proposals, but most will have a limited palette for exterior painting.
Step 2: Evaluate Your Architecture and Materials

Is your condo or townhome modern, colonial, craftsman, or mid-century? Your home’s architectural style should guide your palette. Also consider any brick, stone, or siding features that won’t be painted.
Step 3: Consider Tacoma’s Climate and Lighting
Lighting varies greatly depending on your location. Tacoma’s cloudy skies and evergreen surroundings can mute or enhance certain tones. Test swatches in morning and afternoon light before deciding.
Step 4: Test Paint Samples on the Actual Surface
Paint a few swatches directly onto your exterior walls. View them at different times of day, especially in Tacoma’s often overcast conditions.
Step 5: Coordinate with Neighboring Units
If you’re in a connected building or row of townhomes, avoid selecting the same exact color as your neighbor. Choose a coordinating but distinct tone to preserve visual interest.
Step 6: Submit Your Color Selection for COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA Approval
Even if you’re choosing from the approved palette, always submit your choices to avoid delays or costly repaints. We can help with digital mock-ups or formal proposals as needed.
Our Favorite COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA-Compliant Color Combinations for 2025
If you’re overwhelmed by the choices, here are three safe and stylish color combinations that work well for Tacoma condos and townhomes exterior painting:
1. Alabaster (SW 7008) with Urbane Bronze (SW 7048) Trim
Classic yet bold. Great for traditional buildings with large eaves or trim.
2. Dorian Gray (SW 7017) with Snowbound (SW 7004) Accents
A refined neutral combo with subtle contrast and modern appeal.
3. Evergreen Fog (SW 9130) with Shoji White (SW 7042) Trim
Nature-inspired, soft and sophisticated; perfect for Northwest aesthetics.
